beats.t: The corridor had no visible end. Door-sized cards lined both walls. Every picture moved: wind blowing, stars turning, someone walking.
Is this the tarot sky? Looks like an exhibition. There's no admission fee, right?
If there is, I'll pay. In exchange for your birth date and time.
Someone put something in his mouth.
[ Major Arcana · 0 → 21 ] Proceed in order
The twenty-two Major Arcana form one story: the Fool sets out and travels to the world's end. Skip the order and the doors won't open.
Like a ledger. You have to balance one line before writing the next.
Seo Hanbi walked at the back, three steps behind Yeoni. When Yeoni stopped, so did she. That was how probation was being observed.
Yeoni touched the card in their pocket. Its star-patterned back. The card that still wouldn't turn over felt warm beneath their fingertips.
(He keeps sitting down. Maybe it isn't only his hand that hurts.)
Neo, don't feel like walking? Want a piggyback?
You'd carry me? We have a bit of a height difference now.
Think I can't? Stop bracing on your hands and try leaning on me.
Neo gave Yeoni's back a gentle push and led the way. His footsteps made no sound on the stone. Yeoni thought he was deliberately walking softly.
Before the first card: Zero, the Fool. A young traveler carrying a bundle gazed skyward from a cliff's edge. A small white dog barked at the traveler's feet.
A dog but no otter. Discrimination.
The Fool is a fearless beginning. Taking a step even knowing it's a cliff.
Don't tell me we have to jump too.
Knew it.
The cliff inside the card came toward them. The ground vanished, leaving only clouds. Yeoni reached for Neo's arm and caught empty air.
Oiiink! Isn't there a card that gives advance warning?!
The five fell onto clouds. It didn't hurt. The clouds became the floor of the next card: the Magician's table, Number One.
Four things lay on the table: a cup, a sword, a wand, and a coin. Beside them, an unlit candle. As though lighting it would open the next door.
Fire? My specialty.
Moka took a match from his apron. It lit on the first strike. As the candle caught, the Magician in the picture doffed his hat to Moka.
See that? He greeted me. Me. People in this sky have manners.
You'll need even better manners at Door Two. The High Priestess's room.
Number Two, the High Priestess's room, was silent. A prohibition marked the wall: Whoever speaks must return. Yundal shut his mouth. His expression was agonized.
Yeoni fought a laugh at Yundal's face. Seo Hanbi offered him paper and a pen. He scribbled: Ladies' birth dates and times.
Writing it won't make me tell you.
The moment they left, Yundal took an enormous breath. Far too enormous for someone who'd held back for two minutes.
The longest two minutes of my life.
Number Three, the Empress's wheat field, glowed gold. Ears of grain bowed in the wind. As Seo Hanbi passed, they leaned only toward her, as though scenting water.
I didn't do anything.
Of course grain leans toward someone who brings rain. Good compatibility.
At the top of Number Four, the Emperor's stairs, stood an empty stone throne. Only a voice echoed: What do you govern? Answer, and pass.
My kitchen.
My mouth. Not very successfully.
My ledger. From now on.
Yeoni's turn. After a long moment's thought, they took out their notebook and waved it.
This. I write everything I forget in here. It governs me.

The stone door above the stairs opened. The throne seemed to give a little chuckle. At Number Five, the Hierophant's bell tower, a bell rang three times. Doors opened one by one. Moka lit fires, Yundal read paths, Yeoni answered questions.
Smoother than I expected. At this rate we'll finish all twenty-one cards today.
That's the sort of thing you must never write in a ledger.
Why?
Because the next line always contains an accident.
They decided to rest before Door Six, covered in ivy. Yundal took his own deck from his clothes. The cards were old and worn by use.
While we rest, shall we each draw one? Tarot drawn in the tarot sky is quite accurate.
Me first! No, Moka first.
Why me? No thanks. I don't believe in fortune-telling.
Saying that, Moka was the first to draw. He turned the card over: two naked figures and an angel. Number Six, the Lovers.
Oh. The Lovers. Your partner is probably the person right in front of you, Moka.
You switched that card, didn't you?! Hands out! Gloves off!
Not the glove! There's actually a hole in there!
The two wrestled over a single card. Yeoni laughed, clutching their stomach. After watching them, Seo Hanbi drew one.
Eleven. Someone holding scales.
Justice. It suits you, my lady.
Meaning a card of punishment.
No. Justice is scales, not punishment. Balancing what has tipped. Exactly what you're doing now.
Seo Hanbi didn't answer. She studied the card for a long time, then carefully tucked it into the ledger.
Your turn, Neo. What card will you get?
I'll pass.
No. Everyone drew one. We're traveling as a group.
Neo reached with his right hand. His fingertips passed through the cards. He quickly switched to his left and picked one. Yeoni saw that brief moment.
(His hand just passed through the card. I didn't imagine it.)
Neo laid the card down. Number Eight, Strength. A woman in white soothed a white cat with bared claws using her bare hands. The cat retracted its claws and leaned its head against her.
Strength. Not brute force, but the power to tame. Gentle hands overcoming something fierce.
A cat. Definitely Neo's card.
Look at the woman's face.
Yeoni peered at the card. The woman in the picture lifted her head. She had exactly Yeoni's face. And the forepaw of the cat she stroked was transparent.
Neo. This...
It's a card illustration. It doesn't have to match how we look now.
That night, the cards along the corridor walls went dark one by one. Only Number Eight, Strength, shone white. Wherever its light touched, Neo's body faded.
Neo tried to stand, then sank down. It wasn't only his legs that were transparent now. Light showed through his chest.
This place is unusually sensitive to names.
Neo's knees buckled. Yeoni caught his arm but felt almost no weight. The floor's pattern began showing through parts of his body.
Neo! Stay with me. Hold my shoulder. Slowly. Breathe first.
Neo couldn't gather enough breath to answer. Yeoni draped his arm over their shoulder. His remaining left hand clung to their sleeve.
Lean on me. Stop pretending you're okay. I'll hold you now.
Neo barely managed a nod. He wasn't saving words. Even one word required breath.
The Strength card's light is wearing him away. There's something inside it.
Ketu. The tail is hiding behind the illustration. It eats the past, so it's gnawing at Mr. Cat's past.
Then burn that card!
Burn it and the path breaks. Without passing Number Eight, we can't reach Twenty-One.
The next path lay beyond Door Six. Supporting Neo, Yeoni stopped before the ivy-covered entrance.
Wait. We're going now, with the cat like that? Let's rest for a night.
Resting will wear him away further. Number Eight's light is stronger at night. Going through is the fastest way.
Then I'll stand in front. Whatever is beyond the door, let it hit me first.
You said you have no power.
That's why I'm going first. I have the least to lose.
Yeoni started to speak, then stopped. Instead, they tugged Seo Hanbi's coat once: don't go too far ahead. Seo Hanbi stood only half a step in front.
Then let's get through quickly. Lovers or whatever.
If it's the Lovers, is it a door for confessions? Yundal will ask birthdays again.
Not this time. This door doesn't make you ask. It makes you read.
Read what?
That's the trouble. Each door makes you read one thing: whatever hurts most.
Neo's jaw tightened. Yeoni laid their hand over his where it clung to their sleeve. They couldn't lightly say it would be all right.
The ivy drew back by itself. In the center of the door was a nameplate. The lettering was still blurred. A three-syllable name. Only the first was barely visible: Park.
This door opens only to one who speaks the name. Read the nameplate, vessel.
Neo seized Yeoni's sleeve. His hand shook, as though he had spent every last bit of strength. A very small, urgent voice reached them.
“Don't read it. Yeoni. Not that.”
The second part of the name began to appear. Yeoni couldn't look away. Neo's hand tightened on their sleeve.
